items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Tells it like it is, like it was. I love James.

ctx.x: I was in the – I just finished his book, and I was – I didn’t really know the extent of, in going back, the kind of things – he doesn’t hide anything about . . .
No, he’s just right on it. Tells it like it is, like it was. I love James.
Did Lex have that reputation? Because a lot of cats went through there, and the Tombs too.

items.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: he played in Jimmy Heath’s band when Jimmy Heath had a band in Philadelphia

ctx.x: Yeah, learn that, in the hopes that something will come out of him, you know. And that’s probably why they want to go in other directions. So they go no I don’t think so and they go and they try to skip over that see? They usually did that, they preferred to skip over that, they’ll say we’ll have his sound and then we’ll go and do, but his sound was all that it was.

Yeah he had a whole lot of experience. He did a whole lot of things. You know he played in all kinds of bands, he played in funk bands, he played bebop, he played in big bands, he played in Jimmy Heath’s band when Jimmy Heath had a band in Philadelphia, and he played alto, you know, until he heard Charlie Parker, then he stopped doing that.
Some people say that he played the tenor so high because he really still heard the sounds from the alto, like he was playing everything a fourth up higher.
